questions.question: Explain how meat was shared in a San band and give two reasons why sharing was important.
questions.expected_answer: Meat was shared out according to rules so that every family got a portion, often by the owner of the arrow that made the kill. Sharing meant that no one went hungry, because hunts did not succeed every day, and it kept everyone equal, so no one could become rich or boast.

questions.question: How did San bands make decisions without chiefs?
questions.expected_answer: Decisions were made by talking together until people agreed. Elders and skilled people were respected and listened to, but could not force others to obey. Quarrels were talked out, joked about, or a family moved to another band for a while.

questions.question: Describe two San beliefs.
questions.expected_answer: The San believed in a spirit world alongside the everyday world. The eland was a special animal with great spiritual power, linked to rain and healing. Healers danced into a trance at healing dances to draw out sickness and travel to the spirit world. Some groups told stories about Kaggen, a trickster spirit who could take the form of a praying mantis.
